prompt:
Animate ONLY ONE local reusable patch of ground erupting with infernal volcanic fire, in a fixed top-down/slightly angled dark-fantasy game view. HD pixel art with sharply clustered pixels, dark charcoal rock edges, deep red magma, vivid orange/amber flame, small pale-yellow molten cores. Match the Ash Warden infernal charcoal-and-orange aesthetic. The uploaded image is only the quiet initial ignition state, NOT the peak: make the eruption substantially larger and more explosive.
ONE SHOT, exactly 12 sequential frames: frames 1-2 tiny ground cracks ignite; 3-5 explosive upward eruption and a low crawling expansion across the nearby ground; 6-7 broad fiery tongue at peak intensity; 8-9 collapse into falling molten fragments and embers; 10-11 near-extinguished scattered tiny embers; frame 12 completely empty transparent canvas, including the cracks and all ground fragments. Do not restart the fire at the end. This is not a repeating idle flame.
Fixed 192x192 transparent canvas. Ground contact remains anchored around pixel (96,144). Keep the entire effect, sparks, and fragments inside x=24..168 and y=24..160 with generous transparent padding. Keep a low elliptical ground footprint and upward flames visibly connected to the cracks. Constant pixel density and scale, stable camera, no per-frame zoom.
No character, no boss, no sword, no UI, no text, no backdrop, no opaque floor tile, no detached airborne slash, no beam, no projectile, no full screen wave, no arc, no semicircle. This is a single modular segment for later engine reuse, not an assembled attack. Crisp pixel edges, no blur, no soft smeared fire.
VARIANT C — heavier magma and ember-rich: 85-110 pixel-wide dense molten fissure, thick dark-crimson lava folds under orange fire, slow heavy chunks lifting only a short distance and falling back, more glowing ash and ember fragments. Strong material weight; let every dark rock fragment fade away by frame 12.
